title: Staged release gatekeeper: profile validation + autoswitch for FP8/INT8 serving
creator: Ava Kumar
description: Implement a Gatekeeper service and rollout workflow that validates FP8/INT8 quantization profiles during staged releases and automatically switches traffic back to a safe baseline when quality or stability regressions are detected. This ticket covers profile validation logic, live telemetry checks, automatic traffic switchover, operator visibility, and escape hatches.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New quant profiles (FP8/INT8) can be deployed to a staged release path that routes a configurable fraction of traffic to the quantized variant while the remaining traffic hits the baseline (FP32) or last known-good profile.
2) Gatekeeper continuously evaluates both offline validation set metrics and live telemetry signals (accuracy proxies + safety) and will automatically shift 100% of traffic back to baseline if any hard thresholds are exceeded.
3) Rollouts expose clear operator signals in Console: per-profile metric deltas, time-series, and a single-click emergency rollback button.
4) Failover steps are auditable: Gatekeeper writes signed, immutable events to the audit log and surfaces the cause, timestamps, and affected routes.
5) End-to-end tests cover profile acceptance, synthetic regressions, and autoswitch behavior with injection tests.
6) Integration with existing routing, KV cache, and serving runtime so switching preserves active sessions or issues graceful cancelation as configured.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary-like staged path): Enable staged path in sandbox for a small set of internal customers. Traffic fractions: 1% -> 5% -> 20%.
Phase 2 (metric tuning): Run a week of telemetry validation, tune thresholds.
Phase 3 (pilot): Open to selected production tenants with 5–10% traffic for 48h.
Phase 4 (autoswitch ON): Enable automatic fallback for low-risk models; ops-only for high-risk models for another 2 weeks.
Escape hatch: Manual override and instant redirect to pinned baseline. TTL on autoswitch attempt to prevent oscillation (default 15 min).
observability_requirements:
Expose the following timeseries per deployment:
- calibration_loss (offline holdout),
- embed_cosine_delta (live vs baseline),
- accuracy_delta_pct (top-k, BLEU-like where applicable),
- safety_alert_rate (policy triggers),
- latency_p95 and p99,
- error_rate and NaN_count,
- kv_cache_hit_ratio and memory_pressure.
Gatekeeper should evaluate 1m/5m/15m windows and publish a decision signal with the sampled test-set values attached. All signals are traceable to request ids for root-cause debugging.
validation_thresholds:
Default thresholds (configurable per-profile):
- offline eval accuracy drop > 1.0% relative to baseline => HARD FAIL
- embedding cosine similarity drop > 0.03 => SOFT FAIL
- safety_alert_rate increase > 50% relative => HARD FAIL
- latency_p95 increase > 30% or latency_p99 increase > 50% => SOFT FAIL
- error_rate spike > 0.1% absolute => HARD FAIL
- any NaN or OOV-related runtime exception => IMMEDIATE FAIL
Soft fails trigger alert+traffic slow-down; hard fails trigger autoswitch to baseline.
test_plan:
1) Offline: run profiling across holdout prompt sets for FP32/FP8/INT8 and record metrics.
2) Integration: deploy staged profile to test cluster, run synthetic traffic with introduced perturbations to simulate degradations. Verify Gatekeeper decisions and audit log entries.
3) Chaos: inject runtime faults (increased memory pressure, intentional tokenization edge cases, random NaNs) and confirm immediate fallback.
4) Canary-mirroring: traffic mirror production 1% to validate distribution match.
5) End-to-end regression: automated CI job that validates any PR touching gatekeeper does not regress decision latency beyond 500ms.
implementation_notes:
- Gatekeeper runs as a control-plane service with read-only access to telemetry and write access to routing policy.
- Use signed decision tokens (KMS) so the data-plane can verify a switch came from Gatekeeper.
- Keep per-profile config in runtime-store with immutable profile hashes.
- Add lightweight calibration-extractor in runtime to stream per-request numeric summaries (min/max/quantization-errors) to telemetry pipeline (sample 1/1000 by default).
- Avoid full request payload copying; use existing token sampling hooks.
- Provide feature-flag toggle to require manual approval before autoswitch for high-security tenants.
- Rate-limit autoswitches: backoff doubling with jitter to prevent flip-flopping.
dependencies_notes: Depends on: ENG-74201 (telemetry uniformization) to ensure metrics nomenclature and windows; ENG-79812 (routing API extensions) to perform atomic traffic reweights and honor sticky sessions. Also coordinate with Product for console surfaces and with Security for audit/schema review.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: False positives due to noisy metrics causing unnecessary failovers. Mitigation: require multi-window confirmation (e.g., 3 consecutive 1m windows) for soft thresholds and require paired offline eval regression for certain model classes.
Risk: Autoswitch causes user-visible behavior changes. Mitigation: Add cooldowns, gradual ramp-down, and session-stickiness policies.
Risk: Increased telemetry cost. Mitigation: sample aggressively and cap per-tenant data retention for gatekeeper-related payloads.
notes_for_reviewers:
Focused feedback requested on:
- proposed default thresholds for hard vs soft fails,
- per-profile sampling rates that balance signal vs cost,
- audit log format and retention policy,
- operator UX: what minimum info is needed for a confident manual rollback?
